note: Plain-language text for the information popovers (terms) and the help flyout (screens). Fictional ACME demonstration wording only. The text explains how the demonstration behaves; it states no fee, limit, rule or timing, which come from rules_and_fees.json.

muse_provenance.label: Muse label
muse_provenance.text: Every Muse result carries a label that says where it came from. "Replay" means the stored answer of an earlier run was shown again and no model was called now. "Live" means the model was called for this result. "Cached" means an identical earlier request was answered from the stored result. The label is never hidden.

muse_run.label: Muse run
muse_run.text: One recorded execution of the model task for a case. A run proposes values; it never writes a record. A steward accepts or corrects the proposal and the reviewer decides.

party_record_status.label: Record status
party_record_status.text: Whether the person or organization record itself is active in the master data. It says nothing about any license or registration the record holds.

license_status.label: License or registration status
license_status.text: Whether the license or registration held by the person or organization is valid. An active organization can hold an expired registration; both can be correct.

data_issue.label: Data issue
data_issue.text: A discrepancy that a steward still has to resolve, such as two sources disagreeing. It is shown only when an open issue exists.

source_last_changed.label: Source last changed
source_last_changed.text: The time the source system says it last changed the record. It is separate from the time this application last received or checked it.

match_evidence.label: Evidence before score
match_evidence.text: The agreements and conflicts the matcher found are the evidence. A score only orders the candidates; it is an uncalibrated heuristic and not the chance that two records are the same.

action_preview.label: What this action will do
action_preview.text: A preview of the records an action would link or leave unlinked, the application relationship that would change, which source values are kept and whether an issue would remain. Nothing is written until you press the action.

extraction_checks.label: Extraction checks
extraction_checks.text: Extraction checks test the shape of what Muse returned: the fields are present, the values have the right type and every value cites a place in a document. They say nothing about whether the application meets a rule.

application_checks.label: Application checks
application_checks.text: Application checks are the deterministic rules run against the application itself, for example a setback or a required document. They are separate from the extraction checks, which only test what Muse returned.

record_status.label: Record status
record_status.text: Record status says where a case stands in its own workflow, such as submitted, under review or approved. It is not the same as the status of a credential.

credential_status.label: Credential status
credential_status.text: Credential status says whether a licence or registration shown for a contractor or business is valid on the date that matters. It is checked separately from the record status of a case.

reason_code.label: Reason code
reason_code.text: A reason code is a short typed label for why a case was returned, denied, waived, sent back for revisions or archived. The codes are a fixed list; the free text beside a code adds detail but never replaces it.

distance_from_property_line.label: Distance from the property line
distance_from_property_line.text: How far the structure stands from the edge of the lot, measured on the ground in feet. The rule that applies to this permit type is checked from the value entered here.

content_hash.label: Content hash
content_hash.text: A fingerprint of a stored document. If even one character of the file changes, the fingerprint changes, so it shows that the document the model read is the document on file.

prompt_version.label: Prompt version
prompt_version.text: The version of the instructions given to the model for this task. Two runs with the same prompt version were given the same instructions.

policy_population.label: Population
policy_population.text: The set of cases a what-if is scored on. A synthetic year is a generated sample of a year of cases and is always labelled so. A retrospective re-scoring takes stored cases and scores them again under the rules in force now; it does not rebuild the decisions made at the time.

policy_outcome_counts.label: Counts by outcome
policy_outcome_counts.text: How many cases the adjudication agent would recommend approving, approving with conditions, holding for a person or denying, under today's published rules (baseline) and under the what-if (scenario). The same cases are counted both times. A person decides every case.

policy_flipped.label: Cases that change
policy_flipped.text: A case changes when its rule result, its recommendation or its intake route differs between the baseline and the scenario. Cases are counted once, however many measures moved.

policy_direction.label: Direction
policy_direction.text: Relaxed means the case got a more permissive result under the scenario, for example a denial that becomes an approval. Tightened means the opposite, for example an approval that becomes a hold. The direction is worked out from the recommendation, then the rule result, then the intake route.

policy_safety_signals.label: Safety signals
policy_safety_signals.text: Every case that stops failing a rule is listed with the rule, the value it had and the limit before and after, so a person can judge the risk. A case that stops failing a rule is not a case that is safe; it is a case to look at.

policy_holds.label: Recommendation holds
policy_holds.text: Cases the agent would hold for a person instead of recommending an outcome. A hold cleared is a case the agent would no longer hold. Identity, parcel, credential, finance and missing-input safeguards and the decision itself stay with the people and checks that own them. This counts cases, not time.

policy_needs_information.label: Needs information
policy_needs_information.text: Cases the intake router sends back to early resolution because something required is missing. It is a count of cases at intake, not a measure of time.

policy_service_targets.label: Service targets
policy_service_targets.text: The number of days a permit type is configured to be handled in. The what-if shows the configured figures before and after. No processing time is worked out from them.

policy_hypothetical_fees.label: Hypothetical assessed fees
policy_hypothetical_fees.text: What the published fee schedule arithmetic would assess for the cases in the population, rounded the way real assessments are. They are not money collected and not a forecast of it. Cases without a usable valuation cannot be priced and are listed apart.

policy_unpriceable.label: Cases that cannot be priced
policy_unpriceable.text: A case with no usable valuation, or with no fee schedule in force on its date, cannot be given a fee. It is left out of both totals and listed here with the reason.

policy_content_hash.label: Content hash
policy_content_hash.text: A fingerprint of everything the run holds: the scenario revision, the full baseline and proposed configuration, the cases, the population definition, the analysis moment and the engine and generator versions. It does not include ids or times, so the same inputs always give the same hash.

queue.title: Work queue
queue.purpose: The cases waiting on someone, with the next step named for each.
can_do: Open a case from its row.
Switch between the saved views and filter by department, type or state.
queue.next: Open a case to act on it; what you may change there depends on your persona's grants.

applicants.title: People & organizations
applicants.purpose: One record per person or organization, with where each value comes from.
can_do: Search by name or alias, and filter people or organizations.
Open a record for its overview, sources and history.
Request a correction where your persona may.
applicants.next: A correction goes to the system that owns the value; it is not edited here.

masters.title: Master records
masters.purpose: The master records for people and organizations, properties, business licenses and contractor registrations, each owned by a source system.
can_do: Switch between the four collections with the tabs.
Open a record for its overview, sources and history.
Open source details to see who owns a value and where to change it.
masters.next: To change a value, change it in the system that owns it; a steward can request the correction.

permit.title: Permit workspace
permit.purpose: Everything about one application in one place: the submission, documents, Muse run, findings, decision and history.
can_do: Read the Muse proposal and the findings.
Take the actions your persona is granted; a button that is unavailable says what is missing.
permit.next: A steward resolves findings, the reviewer records the decision, and the permit is issued only when the balance is paid.

steward.title: Data issues
steward.purpose: The steward's work queue: record matches and source problems that need a person to decide. The matcher and Muse propose; the steward decides.
can_do: Filter by Needs review, Assigned to me, Awaiting source or Resolved.
Open an issue to read the evidence, preview what an action will do, and record a decision.
steward.next: The decision is recorded with the evidence and the note, and appears in the history of the record. A permit decision is a separate step.

source_records.title: Source records
source_records.purpose: The accepted records received from each source system, with the master record each one is linked to.
can_do: Filter by source system.
Open source details to see the full identifiers and who owns the source.
source_records.next: To compare a source record with the master records, open the Data issues queue.

activity.title: Activity
activity.purpose: Decisions and changes recorded for the records you steward. It is not the administrator's audit log.
can_do: Read who decided what, when, and the note they gave.
activity.next: Open a record from its link to see its full history.

rules.title: Rules and fees
rules.purpose: The versioned rule sets and fee schedules that checks and assessments use. Synthetic ACME values.
can_do: Read the published rules and fees.
Draft and publish a version where your persona may.
rules.next: A published version applies to new evaluations; earlier decisions keep the version they used.

reconciliation.title: Reconciliation
reconciliation.purpose: Assessments, receipts and allocations for each case.
can_do: Compare what was assessed with what was received.
Record an allocation where your persona may.
reconciliation.next: When the balance is zero, the permit can be issued.

governance.title: Governance and sources
governance.purpose: Who owns each dataset, and what arrived without an owner.
can_do: See the owner and steward of a dataset.
Escalate an issue or reassign a steward where your persona may.
governance.next: An escalated issue waits for the owner named here.

agent_intake.title: Intake agent
agent_intake.purpose: The intake agent reads the received documents and proposes values; it does not decide anything.
can_do: Review its recorded steps.
Run it on a case where your persona may.
agent_intake.next: Its proposal goes to a steward for review.

agent_adjudication.title: Adjudication agent
agent_adjudication.purpose: The adjudication agent recommends an outcome from the rules and the evidence; the reviewer decides.
can_do: Read its recommendation and the evidence it cites.
Confirm or revert a recommendation where your persona may.
agent_adjudication.next: Only a confirmed recommendation can lead to a recorded decision.

admin.title: Administration
admin.purpose: Configuration and persona administration for the demonstration. Configuration never implies a business approval.
can_do: Review the configured actors and settings.
admin.next: Business decisions stay with the personas that hold those grants.

intake_queue.title: Intake queue
intake_queue.purpose: The cases the City has in front of it, in saved views. Search, filter and sort work through the address bar alone.
can_do: Pick a saved view.
Select cases and process them with the agent.
intake_queue.next: Open a case to resolve what the intake left.

early_resolution.title: Early resolution
early_resolution.purpose: The cases that wait for a person, grouped by the finding that puts them here.
can_do: Open a case from its group and resolve the finding.
early_resolution.next: A resolved case moves on to review.

review_queue.title: Review queue
review_queue.purpose: The cases with the Permit Reviewer, by review area, and the decisions recorded recently.
can_do: Open a case to read the recommendation and record a decision.
review_queue.next: A recorded decision is reconfirmed or issued from the case.

apply.title: Start an application
apply.purpose: Choose the kind of project. The portal then asks only for what that kind of project needs.
can_do: Pick a project type to open its application form.
Track an application you already sent.
apply.next: You fill in the form, check what is missing, and submit.

apply_track.title: Track an application
apply_track.purpose: Look up an application by its reference number and see where it stands.
can_do: Enter a reference number.
Open the case to read what the City has asked of you.
apply_track.next: If the City asks for more, the request appears with the case; answer it there.

policy_scenarios.title: What-if
policy_scenarios.purpose: Test a proposed change to the permit rules on a set of cases before anything is changed. Saving or running a what-if never changes a rule, a fee, a permit type or an application.
can_do: Start from a suggestion or save a new what-if.
Add the supported kinds of change and run them on a synthetic year or on stored cases.
policy_scenarios.next: A run is kept as a snapshot; open its results, then its briefing for legislators.

policy_run.title: What-if results
policy_run.purpose: What the what-if would change, counted from the same cases scored twice, with each figure's definition beside it.
can_do: Read the counts by outcome, the cases that change and the safety signals.
Open the legislator briefing.
policy_run.next: The briefing is built from these figures only; a change to the real rules is a separate, approved step.

policy_briefing.title: Legislator briefing
policy_briefing.purpose: A plain-language briefing built only from the typed facts of one run. No model wrote it.
can_do: Read it on screen.
Download it as HTML or Markdown.
policy_briefing.next: A briefing written with Muse is planned for a later release; this one is always available.
